items.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE isolated modular scene sprite of an old CHAIN-LINK WIRE FENCE straight segment for the 2D top-down survival game 潮汐线. Input reference is STYLE ONLY: use its restrained gritty low-resolution pixel art, deliberate square pixel clusters, muted gray-green metal and sparse orange-brown rust, simple upper-left highlights. Do not reproduce any reference object. Subject: a continuous HORIZONTAL left-to-right chain-link security fence panel, with two slender upright galvanized steel posts at the far left and far right, a straight thin horizontal top rail and thin lower tension wire, taut open DIAMOND wire mesh between posts. A single straight strand of barbed wire slightly above top rail with sparse small barb knots, not huge concertina coils. The mesh must have REAL TRANSPARENT HOLES: empty transparent alpha between thin metal wires. Medium/coarse diamond mesh, about 10–12 columns by 5–6 rows, readable when reduced to 64 pixels wide. Mild corrosion at post bases, wire intersections and top clamps. Posts are fixed fence posts with small flat bottom ends, NO freestanding tripod legs, no large feet, no masonry base, no ground. Camera: elevated slightly top-down view consistent with reference sprites, see a tiny top face of post caps and rail, but NO isometric diagonal layout; top and bottom rails must run parallel to horizontal screen axis, both posts same height, no vanishing-point narrowing. A reusable straight fence module, NO gate, no damage holes, no signage, no plants, no people, no other objects. Entire object visible, centered in a wide 3:2 transparent canvas, subject fills 88% of width, comfortable transparent margins around all four edges. Crisp low-resolution sprite artwork intended to become a 64x48 pixel scene asset; no photorealism, no smooth 3D render, no fuzzy shadows or atmospheric effects. Genuine transparent alpha background including all diamond holes, no checkerboard painted into image, no background color, no text, no UI.

items.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Redesign ONE north-south chain-link fence sprite for a STRICT 90-DEGREE TOP-DOWN ORTHOGRAPHIC GAME. Since we look straight down along gravity, the whole upright wire-mesh panel projects EDGE-ON into a VERY THIN STRAIGHT VERTICAL LINE. The user intentionally wants it to look like a line. Show ONLY the narrow TOP surface of the thin galvanized tubular top rail, small clamps, a very thin taut barbed tension wire along the same direction with a few short sparse side-pointing barb prongs. At each endpoint show a SMALL ROUND POST CAP viewed exactly from ABOVE: two identical circular top caps, equal size, both centers at EXACTLY the same screen X coordinate. DO NOT show the upright length of the posts: from above only caps can be seen. The connecting rail must be ruler-straight along screen Y, same width end to end. The tops of mesh wires collapse into the narrow line below the rail; NO visible broad mesh panel, NO diamond lattice spread across the canvas, NO upright pole elevation, NO ladder rungs, NO diagonal receding rail, NO distant smaller post, NO horizontal span. Overall visible shape: a long slender vertical gray-green metallic stroke with two small round endpoint dots and five or six tiny barbs sticking just a little to the sides. Actual scene target: 64 pixels length, main line 1–2 pixels thick, end caps only 3–4 pixels diameter, total width including sparse barbs at most 8–10 logical pixels. Pixel-art treatment consistent with existing survival game sprites: muted gray-green steel, tiny orange-brown rust spots and subdued upper-left highlight on top surface, crisp pixel clusters. Large genuinely TRANSPARENT portrait canvas, one centered vertical segment spanning 80–85% canvas height, lots of transparent empty space on BOTH sides, nothing else. No floor, cast shadow, glow, text, labels, background, border, vignette, or atmosphere. This is a precisely orthographic narrow modular north-south boundary asset, NOT an attractive three-quarter product illustration.

items.prompt: Use case: compositing / precise-object-edit. Combine the TWO supplied transparent sprites into ONE new transparent sprite for a 2D game. Input image 1 is the approved strict top-down NORTH-SOUTH fence: a thin perfectly straight vertical line with small rust clamps, sparse barbs and round endpoint caps. Input image 2 is the approved standalone upright metal support post. BOTH are actual components to reuse, not loose style suggestions. Keep their gray-green metal, orange-brown corrosion and pixel-art texture. Required assembly: put the COMPLETE thin fence segment from image 1 in the UPPER portion, and attach the support post from image 2 DIRECTLY BELOW the LOWER END of the fence. Align the longitudinal centerline of the wire segment and the main shaft of the post on ONE EXACT SCREEN-VERTICAL axis. The top cap of the standalone post is the JOIN where the lower endpoint of the fence meets the post: merge/overlap the fence's small lower cap with the post's top cap, avoiding a double cap or gap. The metal post extends DOWNWARD from this join to the bottom of the assembled sprite. The post's visible length below the join should be around HALF the thin wire segment's length above the join. The support post main shaft should be around TWICE the thin wire rail's thickness. Preserve both upper and lower rusty clamp collars on the post and its small connector stubs. Preserve the original thin fence section, its sparse barbs and its small TOP endpoint cap. The image must show one SINGLE segment-and-lower-post assembly, not multiple variants or two separate objects. IMPORTANT: the UPPER wire portion must REMAIN A NARROW STRAIGHT LINE viewed directly from above; do NOT add broad diamond mesh, sideways fence plane, diagonal perspective, receding posts, foreshortening, ladder rungs or a second panel. The lower support post uses the already supplied upright-post sprite appearance exactly as requested by user; do not replace it with only a dot. Full uncut assembled object on genuinely transparent tall canvas, centered with generous transparent empty space on both sides and modest space above/below, upper-left shading consistent with originals. No ground, shadows outside the object, labels, lettering, background, glow or other objects. Produce only the assembled transparent bitmap.

Single centered complete object, same elevated overhead camera and upper-left light as reference, muted gray-green metal and modest orange-brown rust, crisp low-resolution pixel art with readable simplified silhouette.
